title: Payment Arrangements Servicing Sheet — Calculating the Re-dating Shift
content:
For a plan under Payment Arrangements, the re-dating shift is the number of calendar days by which a returned installment is re-dated.

## Definition

The re-dating shift is the number of calendar days from the scheduled due date carried on the plan's most recent returned installment payment to the installment's new due date. The new due date is the re-dating clock start advanced by the re-dating lead plus the re-dating verification buffer. The re-dating clock starts on the handling date, the re-dating lead is 7 days, the re-dating verification buffer is 0 days, and the lead and buffer are counted in calendar days. The re-dating shift is never more than the type's largest shift of one due-date change; a longer shift is cut to that maximum.

## Inputs and where they are read

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Scheduled due date of the returned installment | The most recent returned installment payment on the plan's installment history (the latest by the date the return was received) |
| Re-dating clock start | The handling date |
| Re-dating lead | 7 days |
| Re-dating verification buffer | 0 days |
| Cap | The arrangement type's largest shift of one due-date change, a product figure of the type |

## Order of the calculation

1. Add the lead and the buffer: 7 days plus 0 days is 7 days.
2. Count that many calendar days forward from the clock start to reach the new due date.
3. Count the calendar days from the returned installment's scheduled due date to the new due date: this is the uncapped shift.
4. Where the uncapped shift is more than the type's largest shift, the re-dating shift is that largest shift; otherwise it is the uncapped shift.

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

The plan's most recent returned installment payment carries a scheduled due date of 3 March, and the handling date is 10 March.

- New due date: 10 March advanced by 7 calendar days is 17 March.
- Uncapped shift: from 3 March to 17 March is 14 calendar days.
- On a type whose largest shift reads 15 days, 14 is within it: the re-dating shift is 14.
- On a type whose largest shift reads 10 days, 14 is cut to 10: the re-dating shift is 10.
